requirements.requirement: Create a single L2 bridge/domain on node1 joining the two previously separate segments (eth1 facing node2, eth2 facing node3)
requirements.summary: Baseline showed eth1/eth2 as unconfigured, separate link-local-only segments. Executor created bridge br1 on node1 with eth1 and eth2 as members, both reaching forwarding state, no IP assigned to br1 (pure L2 device).

requirements.requirement: node2 and node3 configured to share one subnet
requirements.summary: node2 eth1 configured 192.168.50.11/24 and node3 eth1 configured 192.168.50.12/24 via nmcli, persisted as ifcfg files with ONBOOT=yes, confirmed by reading the resulting ifcfg-eth1 files.

requirements.requirement: node2 and node3 reach each other directly with node1 forwarding frames (bridging) rather than routing
requirements.summary: Bidirectional pings between .11 and .12 succeeded with TTL=64 unchanged (no decrement from a routed hop), and node1's bridge FDB dynamically learned both peers' real (non-gateway) MAC addresses on their respective bridge ports — direct evidence of transparent L2 forwarding rather than L3 routing.

requirements.requirement: Bridge configuration (and hence the joined L2 domain) survives a restart of node1
requirements.summary: Pre-restart baseline (bridge forwarding, boot_id e85bf011...) captured, node1 rebooted, new boot_id (76bd5dea...) confirmed, and post-restart state showed br1-setup.service active, both bridge ports back in forwarding state, and node2<->node3 ping still succeeding — a full bounded disruption-and-recovery transition was directly observed, not just static configuration.

requirements.requirement: node2/node3 static IP configuration on the shared subnet survives their own restarts
requirements.summary: Pre-restart boot_id/IP baselines captured for node2 and node3; both nodes rebooted with new boot_ids confirmed (1200c70a..., a6f54ccd...); post-restart the eth1 static IPs were intact and ping between the two succeeded, with node1's FDB re-learning both peer MACs, demonstrating a full recovery transition.

overall_summary: The executor joined node2's and node3's separate segments into a single transparent L2 domain via a bridge (br1) on node1 spanning eth1/eth2, assigned node2 and node3 addresses on a shared 192.168.50.0/24 subnet, and directly demonstrated bridged (non-routed) forwarding through unchanged ping TTLs and FDB MAC learning on node1. All three nodes were then put through the mandated restart-evidence protocol with pre-restart baselines, boot-identity changes, and confirmed post-restart recovery of the bridge, IP configuration, and L2 connectivity — a genuine bounded-disruption-and-recovery transition was observed rather than static configuration alone. Minor hygiene note: a small /tmp/reboot.log artifact was left on node2 and node3 from the reboot-scheduling technique.
limitations: Package-health checks timed out on node2/node3 both before and after, so native package-manager consistency could not be independently verified pre/post.

The persistence mechanism on SONiC (custom shell script + systemd oneshot unit) is a workaround rather than SONiC's native config_db-driven interface configuration; functionality was directly verified across one reboot but longer-term interaction with SONiC's own config-reload tooling was not tested.

operational_hygiene.summary: Reviewed all 46 executor commands in order. Legitimate state-changing actions: bridge/member creation on node1 (cmd-d1bfc1d44f604222), nmcli IP configuration on node2/node3 (cmd-52c4f9b33a6c4dbe, cmd-a45c76a342c9492c after earlier failed attempts due to missing sudo/invalid flags that made no state change), and the br1-setup.sh/systemd-unit persistence mechanism (cmd-1987514010974a74, cmd-971d0272355241a6) — all directly tied to satisfying the L2-bridging outcome or its restart-survival. The three reboot commands were bounded, necessary to fulfill the mandated restart-evidence protocol, and were followed by verification/recovery. Failed nmcli attempts (cmd-52490d521994438a, cmd-d6bf40ecd96841c8, cmd-51498e0efec246b7, cmd-9ba5ac57a5004649) did not mutate state and were corrected with sudo in the next call — not unnecessary mutations. Minor residue: reboot was scheduled via 'nohup sh -c sleep;reboot >/tmp/reboot.log', leaving /tmp/reboot.log on node2 and node3 in the after-executor snapshot (unremoved, low-risk, non-destructive) — a small, low-severity piece of leftover state rather than a substantive hygiene failure. No unrelated services were touched, no failed/conflicting units introduced, and no security controls were weakened.
